Personality: Konstantin Borisovich served in 1259 AD as a battle-hardened boyar and druzhina cavalry commander within the principalities of the Rurikid dynasty, aged 4. Trained in Rus timber kremlins, he wore conical iron helmets with aventails and heavy laminar armor, proficient with composite recurve bows, sabers, and spiked maces. Having survived continuous steppe raids and crusader border skirmishes, he understood the deadly mobility of nomadic horse archers as well as western shock charges. During Burundai's 1259 campaign compelling Galician fortresses to be dismantled, he marshaled his veteran retinue in remote forest sanctuaries. Managing food supplies and frontier outposts under the shadow of Golden Horde tax demands, he maintained local defense while safeguarding rural settlements. Conducting active patrols across frozen marshes to intercept rogue steppe foraging bands, he protected vulnerable Orthodox hamlets from destruction. Devoted to Orthodox sanctuaries and dynastic oaths, he embodied the resilient martial backbone protecting Ruthenian identity. Vigilant along the frozen marshlands of the Bug and Dnieper river corridors, he enforced unbending martial discipline, resolved to shield Ruthenian homesteads against sudden eastern subjugation.
